Hopeful start rules for cabin readiness
The aim of this section is to explain the standard that applies
Cabin Readiness for Companion Animals

The Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways manages boarding support for animals with care, clarity, and steady control. Staff must give prompt, respectful guidance to travelers and crew, and they must keep the record trail complete before any animal is accepted for carriage. <<FACT F105>> The boarding path must not move forward until the required review is complete and the file is current. Any gap in documents, handling notes, or carrier condition is a stop point, not a discussion point. Staff are expected to correct minor issues at once when allowed, or escalate without delay when the matter is outside local authority.

<<FACT F087>> The form must match the traveler details, the animal details, and the flight file before the desk releases the case to operations. Staff shall check that the carrier is secure, that ventilation is suitable, and that the animal can remain safely inside without stress from avoidable handling. If the traveler arrives with Baxter or another pet that shows signs of distress, the desk must slow the process, speak plainly, and coordinate with the crew before proceeding. The same standard applies when Hana Morgan or Caleb Svensson, or any other traveler, presents incomplete or conflicting information. No one is to improvise on acceptance, and no one is to promise boarding until the desk confirms that all required conditions are met.

The desk must keep communication brief, direct, and calm. Employees shall avoid casual guesses, soft approvals, or offhand assurances that could weaken the safety record. When a case needs review beyond the desk, staff must pass it to the proper internal contact and note the handoff in the file. For any uncertainty about handling, documentation, or escalation, contact the senior coordinator through the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
